root_cause.text: The `clk_dif` array in `struct rs9_driver_data` was statically allocated with only 4 slots, but the 9FGV0841 chip supports up to 8 outputs, causing an out-of-bounds write when the driver stores clock hw pointers for outputs 4–7.
root_cause.evidence: The patch increases the array size from `[4]` to `[8]` in the structure definition `struct clk_hw *clk_dif[4];` → `struct clk_hw *clk_dif[8];`. The commit message explicitly states: "The 9FGV0841 has 8 outputs and registers 8 struct clk_hw, make sure there are 8 slots ... else there is going to be out of bounds write".

This field is the last one in the struct after pll_ssc; it can be corrupted by the out-of-bounds write if the write index exceeds 6 (since array indices 4-7 write beyond allocated space).
Though located before the clk_dif array, this field is part of the same structure and the vulnerability highlights insufficient array sizing, which is fundamentally a struct design flaw.
Similar to 'client', this field contributes to the struct definition that is vulnerable due to the undersized clk_dif array.
This field is part of the struct and the chip_info likely contains the output count; the discrepancy between chip_info's output count and the array size is the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: The array is statically allocated with only 4 slots, but the 9FGV0841 chip supports 8 outputs. This causes out-of-bounds writes when storing clock hw pointers for outputs 4–7, directly leading to memory corruption.
This field is located immediately after the clk_dif array in the struct. Out-of-bounds writes into the array (indices 4–7) will overwrite this field, corrupting the pll amplitude configuration.
This field is located after pll_amplitude and can be overwritten by out-of-bounds writes that extend beyond pll_amplitude, corrupting spread spectrum control.
This field is the last one in the struct after pll_ssc. Out-of-bounds writes from the clk_dif array can corrupt this field if the write index exceeds 6, affecting slew rate settings.

Though located before the clk_dif array, this field is part of the same struct. The vulnerability stems from insufficient array sizing, which is a fundamental struct design flaw that could lead to corruption of adjacent fields in memory.
Similar to 'client', this field is part of the struct definition that contains the undersized clk_dif array, contributing to the structural vulnerability.

This field stores chip information, which likely includes the output count. The discrepancy between the chip's output count (8) and the array size (4) is the root cause of the out-of-bounds vulnerability.
